raw_response:
Let me think this through as I sit at my kitchen table before the season starts.

I have 11.6 mu. Cotton is my main crop — always has been here in Quzhou. The soil suits it and the price is usually decent if the weather cooperates. I will put about 7 mu into cotton. The rest I split: 3 mu for wheat in winter and then maize on that same ground in summer (the double crop, everyone around here does it), then a small patch of millet and a small patch of mungbean, about 0.8 mu each. Millet and mungbean we mostly keep for ourselves and some to sell at the market. Mungbean is good because it does not need much fertilizer and fixes its own nitrogen — my father taught me that.

For cotton I use Bt hybrid seed — the bollworm used to eat us alive before this variety came out, and I would never go back. I will apply about 18 kg urea-equivalent N per mu, 9 kg P, 9 kg K. I know some say 15 is enough, but if the cotton looks yellow in July I lose money — better put a little extra. Cotton drinks water, so I will irrigate 4 times from my well: once at planting, then at squaring, flowering, and boll-setting. Cotton needs spraying a lot — aphids, spider mites, bollworm — I count on 6 sprays. I plough deep before cotton, it helps the roots.

For wheat I buy improved seed from the dealer — the stuff like Jimai or Shimai varieties our neighbors grow. 15 kg N, 7 kg P, 6 kg K. Three irrigations — winter, jointing, and grain-fill. Two sprays for aphids and rust. Rotary till after maize is fine.

Maize after wheat — hybrid seed (Zhengdan or similar), no-till into the stubble saves me time and diesel. 16 kg N, 7 kg P, 6 kg K. Two irrigations if the rain is short. Two sprays.

Millet and mungbean I manage light — they are hardy. Millet gets 9 kg N, 4 kg P, 3 kg K, one irrigation, one spray. Mungbean barely needs nitrogen — 4 kg is plenty, 5 kg P, 3 kg K, one irrigation, two sprays because the pod borer is bad some years.

Yields I expect based on last few years: cotton about 270 kg seed cotton per mu, wheat 470, maize 520, millet 220, mungbean 110.

decision.reasoning_summary: Cotton is my main crop at 7 mu — Bt hybrid seed because bollworm would ruin me otherwise, and I fertilize a little heavy (18 N) since yellow cotton in July means lost money. I double-crop 3 mu with wheat then maize, standard for our area, using improved wheat seed and hybrid maize with no-till after wheat to save fuel. Small plots of millet and mungbean (0.8 mu each) are mostly for the family and they do not need much input — mungbean especially since it fixes nitrogen. Well irrigation lets me water cotton 4 times and wheat 3 times, which is what gets the yield. I copy what works for my neighbors and what worked for me last year, adjusting only a little.
